purpose: Anastrozole is used to treat breast cancer in women who have gone through menopause. It is often used after surgery or other treatments to help keep the cancer from coming back. In some cases, it is also used to treat breast cancer that has spread to other parts of the body.
how_it_works: Some breast cancers need the hormone estrogen to grow. Anastrozole works by blocking a natural process in your body that turns other hormones into estrogen, which lowers the amount of estrogen in your body. With less estrogen around, it becomes harder for those cancer cells to grow and spread.
common_side_effects: Because this medicine lowers estrogen levels, many side effects feel like menopause symptoms. These can include hot flashes, joint pain or stiffness, bone pain, muscle aches, feeling tired, mood changes, trouble sleeping, nausea, and headaches. Some people also notice thinning hair or dry skin.
warnings: Anastrozole can weaken your bones over time, raising your risk of osteoporosis and fractures, so your doctor may monitor your bone density. Do not take this medication if you are pregnant, as it can seriously harm an unborn baby. It should not be used by women who have not yet gone through menopause. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, especially tamoxifen, as they should not be taken together.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one 1 mg tablet taken by mouth once a day. You can take it with or without food. Try to take it at the same time each day, and if you miss a dose, just skip it and take your next dose as scheduled — never double up.
